task_2.title: Warn that export plugin will need explicit installation
task_2.description: Poetry 1.7.0 now warns when `poetry export` is used that `poetry-plugin-export` will stop being installed by default in a future release, and adds a configuration switch to suppress that advisory without changing export execution.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that running `poetry export` warns users that `poetry-plugin-export` will no longer be bundled by default in a future Poetry release, while still allowing the warning to be disabled without changing export behavior.

expectation.grounded: When the `export` command is invoked, Poetry should emit a warning on command error output by default to inform users that `poetry-plugin-export` will require explicit installation in a future Poetry version. Poetry should support a boolean `warnings.export` configuration value, defaulting to `true`, and suppress the warning when that setting is `false`. After warning handling, `poetry export` should continue executing the existing export command behavior.
expectation.conceptual: Using the export command should proactively notify users about the upcoming change to plugin bundling, while preserving the current export workflow. Teams that do not want the advisory should be able to turn it off through normal configuration without affecting the command itself.

constraints.grounded: `warnings.export` must be treated as a supported boolean Poetry configuration key. Disabling the warning must only silence the advisory and must not remove, block, or alter `poetry export` execution or output generation. The warning must be scoped to `poetry export` rather than unrelated commands.
constraints.conceptual: This change must remain advisory only. It should not break existing automation, change export results, or surface the notice outside the export flow, and opting out should only suppress the warning.

behavior: `poetry export` now emits a warning on error output before running the export operation when export warnings are enabled.
Poetry now exposes `warnings.export` as a user-configurable boolean setting with a default enabled state.
Setting `warnings.export` to `false` suppresses the export-plugin warning.
The `export` command still delegates to the existing export implementation after the warning check, so the command continues to run normally.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `poetry export` with default configuration, the command should display a warning that the export plugin will need explicit installation in a future Poetry release and then continue running the export command.
When a user disables `warnings.export` and runs `poetry export`, the command should not display the plugin-installation warning.
When a user inspects or sets Poetry configuration, `warnings.export` should be recognized as a valid boolean setting with a default enabled value.
When a user runs Poetry commands other than `export`, they should not receive this export-plugin warning.

task_3.title: Add Poetry post-checkout and post-merge install hook
task_3.description: Poetry 1.7.0 adds a new pre-commit hook, `poetry-install`, so projects can automatically run dependency installation after checkout and merge events and keep environments aligned with the lock file when branches change.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Poetry exposes a `poetry-install` pre-commit hook that users can enable to refresh installed dependencies after checkout and merge events so branch changes do not leave the environment out of sync with the lock file.

expectation.grounded: Poetry 1.7.0 should publish a pre-commit hook with id `poetry-install`. The hook must invoke the `poetry install` command, accept the same command-line arguments as `poetry install`, and be installable for hook types that cover checkout and merge events. Its user-facing purpose is to keep locked dependencies installed after branch or checkout changes.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to opt into an official Poetry hook that automatically reinstalls project dependencies after repository state changes, reducing manual dependency resync work when switching branches or merging changes.

constraints.grounded: The new capability must be additive to the existing Poetry hook set, must not depend on changed filenames to execute, and must remain limited to the documented checkout and merge lifecycle usage rather than altering the behavior of normal pre-commit validation hooks. Hook consumers must be able to pass supported `poetry install` options through the hook configuration.
constraints.conceptual: The feature should behave like an optional automation layer for dependency synchronization, without changing existing hook workflows or requiring unrelated repository changes to trigger it.

behavior: A new official pre-commit hook named `poetry-install` is available to configure in `.pre-commit-config.yaml`.
When installed for checkout and merge lifecycle events, `poetry-install` runs automatically after those events instead of waiting for staged file matching.
The hook executes `poetry install` to bring the environment in line with the current lock file state.
Projects may supply the same arguments they would pass to `poetry install`, including directory-selection arguments for non-root project layouts.
acceptance_criteria: When a project references the Poetry hook repository for version 1.7.0 and configures `id: poetry-install`, the hook should be recognized as a valid hook id.
When the hook is installed for checkout and merge events, switching branches or completing a merge should trigger Poetry dependency installation automatically.
When the hook runs, it should use the current project's lock file to install locked packages rather than acting as a generic validation-only hook.
When hook arguments are provided, the hook should forward them using `poetry install` semantics so monorepo and custom-install use cases remain configurable.

task_4.title: Add prerelease phase advancement to `poetry version`
task_4.description: Poetry 1.7.0 adds a `--next-phase` option to `poetry version`. When used with the `prerelease` rule on an already unstable version, it advances the prerelease phase instead of only incrementing the current prerelease number, allowing alpha versions to move to beta, beta versions to move to release candidates, and release candidates to become final releases.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `poetry version` lets users advance an existing prerelease to its next phase with `--next-phase` when running the `prerelease` update rule, including progressing from alpha to beta, beta to release candidate, and release candidate to the final release.

expectation.grounded: The `poetry version` command must accept a `--next-phase` option. When the requested rule is `prerelease` and the current package version is already unstable, `poetry version prerelease --next-phase` must advance the prerelease phase rather than incrementing the numeric suffix within the same phase. Advancing phase must restart the prerelease counter for alpha, beta, and release-candidate transitions, and advancing from a release-candidate version must yield the corresponding stable release. Existing `poetry version prerelease` behavior without `--next-phase` must continue to increment the current prerelease number.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to choose between continuing the current prerelease series and promoting the version to the next prerelease stage. Promotion should follow the normal prerelease lifecycle and produce a final stable version when promoting a release candidate.

constraints.grounded: `--next-phase` must not change version bump behavior for non-`prerelease` rules. For `prerelease` on a version that is not already unstable, the command must retain the normal first-prerelease behavior rather than skipping directly to a later phase. The command's existing output and version-application flow must remain compatible with the new option.
constraints.conceptual: The new flag should be additive and narrowly scoped. It should only affect prerelease promotion semantics, preserve existing behavior in all other versioning cases, and avoid changing how the command otherwise reports or applies version updates.

behavior: `poetry version` exposes a new `--next-phase` option.
When `prerelease` is requested for an already unstable version and `--next-phase` is not provided, the command continues incrementing the prerelease number within the same phase.
When `prerelease` is requested for an already unstable version and `--next-phase` is provided, the command advances the prerelease phase instead of incrementing within the current phase.
Promoting an alpha prerelease with `--next-phase` produces the corresponding beta prerelease with its counter restarted.
Promoting a beta prerelease with `--next-phase` produces the corresponding release-candidate prerelease with its counter restarted.
Promoting a release-candidate prerelease with `--next-phase` produces the corresponding stable release with no prerelease segment.
When the current version is stable, `prerelease` continues to create the first prerelease for the next patch release, regardless of whether `--next-phase` is supplied.
acceptance_criteria: When a project is at an alpha prerelease and the user runs `poetry version prerelease --next-phase`, it should update to the matching beta prerelease instead of incrementing the alpha number.

When a project is at a beta prerelease and the user runs `poetry version prerelease --next-phase`, it should update to the matching release-candidate prerelease instead of incrementing the beta number.
When a project is at a release-candidate prerelease and the user runs `poetry version prerelease --next-phase`, it should update to the corresponding final release.
When a project is at an unstable prerelease and the user runs `poetry version prerelease` without `--next-phase`, it should keep the same prerelease phase and increment that phase's numeric suffix.
When the user runs `poetry version` with any rule other than `prerelease`, the presence or absence of `--next-phase` should not alter the resulting version bump semantics.

When the current project version is stable and the user runs `poetry version prerelease`, it should continue to create the normal first prerelease for the next patch release rather than promoting to a later phase.

task_1.title: Official Python 3.12 compatibility for build and environment workflows
task_1.description: Poetry 1.7.0 adds official Python 3.12 support by updating environment provisioning, isolated build and metadata generation, archive extraction, and forced cleanup behavior to match Python 3.12 and newer build-tool interfaces.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Poetry officially supports Python 3.12 for project installation and package inspection workflows. Ensure that virtual environment creation, isolated PEP 517 builds, source archive extraction, and cleanup behavior continue to work correctly when Python 3.12 changes default packaging tool availability and standard-library APIs.

expectation.grounded: Python 3.12 support must cover `EnvManager.build_venv`, `ephemeral_environment`, `get_pep517_metadata`, and `Chef`-driven build workflows. `EnvManager.build_venv` must accept `str | bool` flag values so explicit `wheel` and `setuptools` requests can be passed as bundled options while still supporting `no-pip`, `no-wheel`, and `no-setuptools`. PEP 517 metadata and build flows must use Python 3.12-compatible `build` interfaces such as `DefaultIsolatedEnv`, `python_executable`, and `source_dir`, and the isolated environment must expose its scripts directory on `PATH` for build requirement installation. Source archive handling used during installation and inspection must continue to extract zip and tar-based archives, including `.tar.gz` and `.tar.bz2`, and tar extraction should use the runtime's safe data-filtered mode when available. Forced directory removal must remain functional on Python 3.12 despite the changed `shutil.rmtree` callback API.
expectation.conceptual: Running Poetry on Python 3.12 should be fully supported across environment creation, source installs, and metadata/build preparation. Build environments should initialize correctly, package metadata generation should succeed, archive-based packages should still unpack normally, and explicit requests for packaging tools such as `setuptools` and `wheel` should continue to work even though newer Python environments no longer assume those tools are preinstalled.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress support for zip archives or tar archives normalized as `.tar.gz` and `.tar.bz2`. Preserve symlink-safe directory removal semantics. Do not implicitly assume `pip`, `wheel`, or `setuptools` are present unless requested, but explicit requests for `wheel` and `setuptools` must still provision them. Maintain compatibility with runtimes that do not provide tar extraction filtering or the Python 3.12 `shutil.rmtree` callback name.
constraints.conceptual: Existing installation and inspection flows must keep working for supported archive formats and previously supported Python runtimes. Cleanup must remain safe, and the upgrade must not silently change packaging-tool availability beyond making explicit provisioning work correctly on Python 3.12.

behavior: `EnvManager.build_venv` accepts flag values beyond booleans so callers can request bundled `wheel` or `setuptools`, and those values are emitted as `--flag=value` style virtualenv arguments.

Virtual environment creation defaults to excluding `pip`, `wheel`, and `setuptools` unless they are explicitly requested, and explicit `with_wheel` or `with_setuptools` requests map to bundled provisioning instead of boolean negation flags.

`get_pep517_metadata` creates its ephemeral environment with `pip` plus bundled `setuptools` and `wheel`, and uses the newer `build` API names needed for Python 3.12-compatible isolated metadata generation.

Isolated build environments used by `Chef` expose their scripts directory on `PATH` and pass `python_executable` to the build backend so build-system requirements can be installed and invoked correctly.

Archive extraction used during installation and inspection is centralized, continues to support zip and tar-based source archives, preserves `.tar.bz2` handling, and applies tar's safe data filter when the runtime supports it.
`remove_directory(path, force=True)` keeps forced cleanup working across Python versions by using the appropriate `shutil.rmtree` callback name while still unlinking symlinks directly.
acceptance_criteria: When Poetry runs under Python 3.12 and creates an isolated environment for PEP 517 metadata generation or builds, it should successfully provision and use the build backend without relying on deprecated `build` APIs.

When a caller explicitly requests `wheel` or `setuptools` during virtual environment creation, the created environment should include those tools on Python 3.12; when they are not requested, Poetry should not assume they are present by default.

When Poetry installs or inspects a package from a `.zip`, `.tar.gz`, or `.tar.bz2` source archive, it should extract the archive successfully and continue package discovery or build preparation normally.

When forced directory cleanup is invoked on Python 3.12, cleanup of stubborn directories should still complete successfully instead of failing because of the updated `shutil.rmtree` callback behavior.

task_5.title: Warn on non-fatal file overwrites during wheel installation
task_5.description: Package installation should no longer silently overwrite an existing installed file. The installer should surface the conflict as a warning while still completing installs that rely on shared namespace-package files, and it should apply per-wheel header destinations and configured bytecode compilation settings consistently for each wheel.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that installing a wheel no longer silently overwrites an existing installed file, that the overwrite is surfaced as a warning without turning compatible namespace-package installs into failures, and that each wheel installation uses its own distribution-specific installation context.

expectation.grounded: During `WheelInstaller.install()`, if `WheelDestination` resolves a target path that already exists, installation should emit a warning through logging and continue rather than raising an overwrite error. For each installed wheel, the destination should be created from the current environment paths with the `headers` scheme rooted under the environment include path plus that wheel's distribution name, and any bytecode-compilation setting previously enabled through `enable_bytecode_compilation()` should be applied to that install.
expectation.conceptual: When a package install would replace an existing file, the package manager should warn the user instead of silently proceeding with no signal. That warning should be non-fatal so installs that depend on shared namespace-package files still work, and each wheel should be installed with its own package-specific destination so headers and optional bytecode compilation are handled consistently.

constraints.grounded: Existing-file conflicts must remain non-fatal and must not be converted into installation errors. Installing multiple wheels with the same `WheelInstaller` instance must not leak destination state across installs: header placement must be derived from the current wheel's distribution, and bytecode optimization levels must reflect the installer's current setting for every new install.
constraints.conceptual: Increase visibility into file conflicts without making previously valid namespace-package installations fail. Repeated installs in one session should not reuse another package's output paths or drop the currently selected compilation behavior.

behavior: If a wheel writes to a target path that already exists, installation emits a warning before overwriting that file.
The overwrite warning is informational only; installation still proceeds instead of failing on the existing file.
Each call to install a wheel creates a fresh destination context based on the current environment paths rather than reusing one mutable destination across wheels.
Header files for a wheel are placed under the include path for that wheel's own distribution name.
When bytecode compilation has been enabled on the installer, that setting is applied to each newly created wheel installation destination.
acceptance_criteria: When installing a wheel that targets a file path that already exists, the install should complete and emit a warning indicating that an existing file is being overwritten.
When the existing file is part of a namespace-package layout, the install should still succeed rather than failing solely because the file already exists.
When multiple wheels are installed sequentially with the same installer, each wheel's header artifacts should be placed under that wheel's own distribution-specific include directory.
When bytecode compilation is enabled before installing wheels, subsequent wheel installs should honor that compilation setting.

task_6.title: Warn when the current project cannot be installed during poetry install
task_6.description: Poetry 1.7.0 makes root-project installation failures visible during `poetry install`. If dependencies can be installed but the current project cannot be installed in editable mode because required package metadata or files are missing, the command now warns the user instead of failing silently, while preserving the existing successful exit behavior and the ability to skip root installation with `--no-root`.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `poetry install` informs users when the current project cannot be installed as part of the install flow, instead of silently succeeding without installing the project itself.

expectation.grounded: `poetry install` should continue attempting to install the current project by default. If current-project installation fails with `ModuleOrPackageNotFound` or `FileNotFoundError`, the command should emit a warning indicating that the current project was not installed and point users to `--no-root` as the supported way to skip root installation, while still returning exit status `0`.
expectation.conceptual: Running the install command without opting out should tell users when only the dependencies were installed and the project itself could not be installed. This should be communicated as a warning, not as a hard failure, and users should be reminded that skipping project installation intentionally is supported.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the behavior of `--no-root`. Do not convert these current-project installation failures into raised command errors or non-zero exit codes. Preserve normal install output when the current project installs successfully.
constraints.conceptual: Intentional dependency-only installs must remain unaffected, successful installs must stay quiet, and the new visibility for root-install problems must not break existing automation that depends on a successful install command.

behavior: When Poetry attempts to install the current project during `poetry install`, installability failures that surface as `ModuleOrPackageNotFound` are no longer silent and are reported as warnings.
Missing files needed by the current project's installation metadata, surfaced as `FileNotFoundError`, are also reported as warnings during `poetry install`.
After warning about the current project's failed installation, the command still completes successfully with exit status `0`.
If `--no-root` is supplied, Poetry continues to skip installation of the current project and does not enter this warning path.
If the current project installs successfully, Poetry continues its normal success flow without emitting the warning.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `poetry install` for a project whose package or module cannot be found, the command should finish with exit status `0` and warn that the current project could not be installed.

When a user runs `poetry install` for a project that references a required file for installation metadata that does not exist, the command should finish with exit status `0` and warn that the current project could not be installed.
When a user runs `poetry install --no-root`, the command should skip current-project installation and should not emit the current-project installation warning.
When a user runs `poetry install` for an installable project, the command should complete without the warning and should continue reporting the current project installation normally.

task_7.title: Expose underlying build-backend errors in Poetry output
task_7.description: In the 1.6.0 to 1.7.0 upgrade, Poetry improves build failure diagnostics by surfacing the original exception wrapped by BuildBackendException, including non-subprocess backend failures, and by updating the suggested pip reproduction command to disable cache. This makes dependency build errors easier for users to diagnose without changing successful install behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Poetry surfaces the underlying cause of package build-backend failures so users can diagnose installation errors without losing the original backend exception context.

expectation.grounded: When Poetry handles a BuildBackendException during package build/install work, the resulting ChefBuildError and user-visible installation output should preserve the backend failure summary and include the wrapped exception details. If the wrapped exception is a CalledProcessError, Poetry should show decoded backend process output, preferring stderr and falling back to stdout when stderr is unavailable. If the wrapped exception is any other exception type, Poetry should show that inner exception's string form instead of hiding it behind the wrapper alone. The follow-up guidance displayed for ChefBuildError should use a pip wheel reproduction command with --no-cache-dir --use-pep517, and should include --editable when the package is being installed in editable mode.
expectation.conceptual: Users should see the real reason a dependency build backend failed, whether the backend failed through a subprocess or by raising a normal Python exception directly. Poetry should continue to present the failure as a backend-originated problem while giving users an updated pip command they can run to reproduce the issue outside Poetry.

constraints.grounded: Do not remove the existing BuildBackendException summary from the reported error; the underlying cause should augment it. Preserve the existing stderr-before-stdout behavior for subprocess-backed failures, keep editable and non-editable reproduction guidance aligned with the package mode, and avoid changing normal behavior for successful builds or non-build-related failures.
constraints.conceptual: This update should only make backend build failures more informative. It should not change how successful installs behave, and it should not reclassify backend problems as Poetry-internal errors.

behavior: Poetry now includes the inner exception associated with a BuildBackendException in the surfaced build failure output instead of reporting only the wrapper-level backend error.
When the wrapped backend failure is a CalledProcessError, Poetry shows decoded process output from stderr when available, otherwise from stdout.
When the wrapped backend failure is not a CalledProcessError, Poetry shows the wrapped exception's text so direct Python errors from the backend are visible to the user.
The diagnostic note shown with ChefBuildError now recommends reproducing the failure with pip wheel --no-cache-dir --use-pep517, and adds --editable for editable dependencies.
acceptance_criteria: When a dependency build backend raises BuildBackendException wrapping a non-subprocess exception, the installation failure shown to the user should include both the backend failure summary and the wrapped exception text.

When a dependency build backend raises BuildBackendException wrapping a CalledProcessError with backend output, the installation failure shown to the user should display decoded stderr output, or stdout if stderr is not available.

When Poetry reports a ChefBuildError for a backend build failure, it should still indicate that the failure likely originates from the build backend and provide a pip wheel reproduction command using --no-cache-dir --use-pep517, adding --editable for editable installs.
When package installation succeeds and no build-backend failure occurs, this upgrade should not alter observable install behavior.

task_8.title: Use a Poetry-specific User-Agent for repository HTTP requests
task_8.description: Poetry 1.7.0 changes repository HTTP requests to identify themselves as Poetry instead of the default requests client so lock, install, and similar package operations are less likely to be blocked by bot protection on private or protected servers.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Poetry's HTTP requests to package repositories identify themselves as Poetry rather than the default generic requests client so dependency operations are not incorrectly blocked as bot traffic.

expectation.grounded: Sessions created for repository access through Poetry's Authenticator should send a User-Agent header that identifies Poetry and its current version, instead of relying on requests' default User-Agent. This header should be present for HTTP traffic issued through those sessions during package resolution and installation flows.
expectation.conceptual: Repository and package-download requests should clearly identify the client as Poetry so servers can distinguish normal package-manager traffic from generic automated traffic.

constraints.grounded: The change should affect the outgoing User-Agent on Authenticator-managed HTTP sessions only and should continue to apply whether the session is returned directly or wrapped with caching behavior. Existing authentication, session creation, and repository access flows should otherwise remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: Only the client identity presented to servers should change; normal repository access behavior should remain compatible with prior versions.

behavior: Poetry initializes a product-specific User-Agent value tied to the running Poetry version for repository HTTP usage.
Every new HTTP session created for repository access sets its User-Agent header before any optional caching adapters are applied.
Outgoing repository requests now advertise Poetry as the client instead of the generic python-requests agent.
Package operations that depend on repository HTTP access are less likely to be rejected by servers that filter or block bot-like default user agents.
acceptance_criteria: When Poetry creates an HTTP session for repository communication, requests sent through that session should include a User-Agent that identifies Poetry and its version.
When dependency lock or install operations contact a repository over HTTP, the requests should no longer present the default generic requests user agent.
When repository sessions are created with or without HTTP caching enabled, the same Poetry-identifying User-Agent behavior should be preserved.

When a repository or proxy applies bot protection based on generic client signatures, Poetry's repository requests should be compatible with a Poetry-specific User-Agent rather than being identified as raw requests traffic.

task_9.title: Make setuptools and wheel opt-in for Poetry virtual environments
task_9.description: Poetry 1.7.0 changes virtual environment provisioning to align with Python 3.12 packaging behavior. Newly created environments no longer assume setuptools is installed by default, and wheel is no longer implied when pip is enabled. Workflows that need packaging helpers, such as PEP 517 metadata inspection, must explicitly provision bundled setuptools and wheel so build metadata continues to work.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading from 1.6.0 to 1.7.0 no longer relies on Poetry-created environments containing setuptools by default on Python 3.12, and ensure that packaging-related workflows still receive setuptools and wheel only when those tools are explicitly required.

expectation.grounded: Poetry environment creation should treat setuptools and wheel as opt-in packages. `EnvManager.build_venv` should only include them when `with_setuptools` or `with_wheel` is explicitly enabled, or when equivalent explicit environment flags request bundled installation; enabling pip alone should not imply wheel. Internal PEP 517 metadata inspection through `get_pep517_metadata` must still run inside an ephemeral environment that includes pip together with bundled setuptools and wheel so metadata generation remains functional on Python 3.12.
expectation.conceptual: After the upgrade, Poetry-managed environments should not silently include legacy packaging helpers by default. Users should only get setuptools or wheel when a workflow explicitly asks for them, while package metadata and build-related operations continue to work without extra manual intervention.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress explicit requests for pip, setuptools, or wheel. Supplying pip should continue to install pip itself, but should not automatically add wheel or setuptools. Explicit opt-in requests for setuptools or wheel must remain honored, and metadata inspection must keep working even though default environments are leaner.
constraints.conceptual: Keep default environments minimal without breaking workflows that intentionally request packaging tools or depend on Poetry's package inspection behavior.

behavior: Poetry-created virtual environments now default to excluding setuptools.
Installing pip into a Poetry-created virtual environment no longer implicitly installs wheel.
Setuptools and wheel are installed only when they are explicitly requested for that environment.
Poetry's temporary environment for PEP 517 metadata extraction explicitly includes pip, setuptools, and wheel so metadata inspection still succeeds on Python 3.12.
Environment creation now supports explicit non-boolean package tool selection semantics for bundled setuptools and wheel instead of relying on disabled-flag inversion.
acceptance_criteria: When Poetry creates a virtual environment with default settings on Python 3.12, the environment should not contain setuptools by default.

When Poetry creates a virtual environment with pip enabled but without an explicit request for wheel or setuptools, the environment should contain pip and should not automatically add wheel or setuptools.
When a caller explicitly requests setuptools or wheel for a Poetry-created virtual environment, the resulting environment should include the requested packaging tool.
When Poetry performs PEP 517 package metadata inspection, it should still complete successfully because the temporary build environment includes the packaging tools required by that workflow.

task_11.title: Sync should remove unmanaged setuptools and wheel
task_11.description: Poetry 1.7.0 makes environment synchronization stricter by no longer preserving `setuptools` and `wheel` as special cases during `poetry install --sync`. If those packages are not required by the project, synchronization should remove them, while still avoiding unnecessary removal of unmanaged `pip`.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `poetry install --sync` fully synchronizes an environment by removing installed `setuptools` and `wheel` when they are not required by the project, instead of preserving them as special cases.

expectation.grounded: When `poetry install --sync` compares installed packages against the packages managed for the project, `setuptools` and `wheel` should be treated like ordinary installed packages: if they are installed but not required by the project, they should be selected for removal. `pip` remains the only packaging-related package that may stay implicitly preserved when it is not managed by the project.
expectation.conceptual: `poetry install --sync` should leave the environment matching the project's actual dependencies. Extra copies of `setuptools` and `wheel` should be cleaned up unless the project depends on them, while unmanaged `pip` should continue to be left alone.

constraints.grounded: Do not remove `setuptools` or `wheel` when they are part of the project's managed package set. Continue preserving unmanaged `pip` during synchronization, and do not change the existing rule that managed packages present in the synchronized result remain installed.
constraints.conceptual: Synchronization must not delete dependencies the project actually needs, and it must keep the existing exception that avoids stripping an unmanaged `pip` from the environment.

behavior: `poetry install --sync` no longer grants implicit keep behavior to installed `setuptools`.
`poetry install --sync` no longer grants implicit keep behavior to installed `wheel`.
During synchronization, installed `setuptools` and `wheel` are removed when they are not required by the project.
During synchronization, unmanaged `pip` remains preserved as the sole packaging tool exempt from removal by default.
If `setuptools` or `wheel` are required by the project and therefore part of the synchronized package set, they remain installed.
acceptance_criteria: When an environment contains `setuptools` or `wheel` but the project does not require them, running `poetry install --sync` should remove those packages.
When a project requires `setuptools` or `wheel`, running `poetry install --sync` should keep them installed.
When an environment contains `pip` that is not managed by the project, running `poetry install --sync` should not remove `pip` solely because it is unmanaged.
When synchronization completes, the installed environment should match the project's managed dependencies plus any still-preserved unmanaged `pip`.

task_10.title: Stop seeding wheel by default in Poetry environments
task_10.description: Poetry 1.7.0 changes virtual environment bootstrapping so `wheel` is no longer installed implicitly. Environments only receive `wheel` or `setuptools` when they are explicitly requested, while package metadata build environments continue to provision the standard build tools they need.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to Poetry 1.7.0 does not assume `wheel` is present in newly created Poetry-managed virtual environments by default, while still allowing explicit opt-in for `wheel` and `setuptools` and preserving metadata/build workflows that require those tools.

expectation.grounded: Poetry-managed virtual environment creation must stop installing `wheel` as an implicit side effect of default creation or enabling `pip`. `wheel` and `setuptools` should only be present when explicitly requested through the environment creation interface, and those explicit requests must still succeed. Temporary environments used for PEP 517 package metadata generation must continue to include `wheel` and `setuptools` so metadata extraction remains functional.
expectation.conceptual: After the upgrade, a new Poetry environment should be leaner by default and should not include `wheel` unless it is explicitly requested. If `wheel` or `setuptools` is requested, the environment should still provide them, and packaging metadata workflows should continue to work without extra user intervention.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress explicit seeding controls for `pip`, `wheel`, or `setuptools`: disabling one of these packages must still omit it, explicitly enabling `wheel` or `setuptools` must still install it, and enabling `pip` alone must not reintroduce implicit `wheel` installation.
constraints.conceptual: The change should only alter the default presence of helper packages. Explicit opt-in or opt-out behavior for environment seed packages should remain predictable, and upgrade-related packaging workflows should keep working.

behavior: Creating a Poetry-managed virtual environment with default seed settings omits `wheel`.
Requesting `pip` for a new environment no longer causes `wheel` to be installed automatically.
Explicitly requesting `wheel` provisions `wheel` in the created environment.
Explicitly requesting `setuptools` provisions `setuptools` in the created environment.
Poetry's temporary environment for PEP 517 package metadata generation continues to provide both `wheel` and `setuptools`.
acceptance_criteria: When a new Poetry-managed virtual environment is created with default settings, it should not contain `wheel`.
When a new Poetry-managed virtual environment is created with `pip` enabled but without an explicit `wheel` request, it should contain `pip` and still omit `wheel`.
When environment creation explicitly requests `wheel`, the resulting environment should contain `wheel`.
When environment creation explicitly requests `setuptools`, the resulting environment should contain `setuptools`.

When Poetry performs PEP 517 metadata extraction for a package that relies on standard build helpers, it should continue to complete without depending on `wheel` being present by default in ordinary Poetry-created environments.

task_13.title: Gracefully handle locked and failing keyring credential lookups
task_13.description: The 1.7.0 update hardens Poetry's keyring integration so credential lookup no longer aborts when the keyring backend is locked or raises access errors. Instead, those failures are treated as an unavailable credential lookup, with normal behavior preserved when a credential is successfully returned.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that keyring-backed credential lookup does not raise user-visible failures when secure storage is locked or the keyring backend errors, and instead continues as if no stored credential was available unless another lookup succeeds.

expectation.grounded: When `PoetryKeyring.get_credential()` calls `keyring.get_credential()` across candidate service names, it should catch `KeyringLocked`, other `KeyringError` failures, and `RuntimeError` raised during credential retrieval. These exceptions should not propagate from credential lookup; the lookup should continue to later candidate names and only return an `HTTPAuthCredential` when a credential is actually obtained. Locked and failed access attempts should be recorded through debug logging.
expectation.conceptual: Credential retrieval through the keyring should degrade gracefully when the backend is temporarily locked or otherwise fails during access. Instead of terminating the operation, the application should treat that lookup as unavailable, continue any remaining credential search, and keep successful credential-based authentication behavior unchanged.

constraints.grounded: Successful keyring reads must still produce the same `HTTPAuthCredential` result as before. The non-fatal fallback applies specifically to credential retrieval failures of type `KeyringLocked`, `KeyringError`, and `RuntimeError`; unrelated keyring behaviors outside this read path should not be broadened by the change.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must preserve normal authentication behavior when credentials are present and should only suppress recoverable keyring-read failures, not hide unrelated problems or alter successful lookups.

behavior: `PoetryKeyring.get_credential()` no longer fails the overall lookup when a keyring backend raises `KeyringLocked` during credential access.
`PoetryKeyring.get_credential()` also suppresses `KeyringError` and `RuntimeError` raised by the backend during credential access.
If one candidate keyring service name fails during lookup, later candidate names are still checked instead of aborting the search immediately.
A locked or failing keyring access is surfaced only through debug-level logging, and the observable credential result for that failed attempt is equivalent to no credential being available.
acceptance_criteria: When credential lookup reaches a keyring backend that raises `KeyringLocked`, the operation should not surface that exception to the caller and should continue as an unavailable credential lookup.
When credential lookup raises `KeyringError` or `RuntimeError`, it should follow the same non-fatal fallback behavior rather than failing the user-facing operation.
When multiple candidate service names are checked and an earlier candidate raises one of those handled errors, later candidates should still be eligible to provide a usable credential.
When the keyring returns a credential successfully, authentication should behave the same as before the upgrade.
When keyring access is locked or fails, diagnostic output should be limited to debug logging rather than a visible runtime failure.

task_12.title: Improve PEP 517 troubleshooting guidance
task_12.description: Poetry 1.7.0 refines the user-facing guidance shown after PEP 517-related build failures so users verify package compatibility with pip caching disabled, reducing misleading successes caused by cached build artifacts.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users who hit a package build failure related to PEP 517 support are told to verify the package with pip caching disabled, so cached artifacts do not make an unsupported package appear to work.

expectation.grounded: When Poetry surfaces its PEP 517 verification guidance after a build-backend failure, the suggested `pip wheel` command should include cache bypassing together with PEP 517 mode. The recommendation should continue to preserve the correct package reference, and editable installs should still be shown in editable form.
expectation.conceptual: When Poetry asks the user to confirm whether a failing package truly supports PEP 517 builds, the guidance should tell them to rerun the check without pip cache so the result reflects the real build behavior.

constraints.grounded: Change only the troubleshooting guidance emitted for the PEP 517-related build failure path. Do not alter which failures trigger the guidance, how install and build operations run, or whether editable versus non-editable package references are distinguished.
constraints.conceptual: Improve the reliability of the troubleshooting advice without changing the underlying install outcome or the general shape of the error flow.

behavior: The PEP 517 troubleshooting output now recommends a `pip wheel` verification command that disables pip cache.
The cache-bypassing recommendation applies to both regular and editable package build failures.
Editable package guidance still indicates an editable verification command, while non-editable guidance continues to point at the package reference being built.
acceptance_criteria: When Poetry reports that a package build may not support PEP 517 and shows a verification command, the command should instruct the user to bypass pip cache.
When the failing package is being installed in editable mode, the suggested verification command should remain editable and also disable pip cache.
When the failing package is a regular dependency, the suggested verification command should keep the non-editable package reference and disable pip cache.

task_14.title: Preserve descriptions for setup-based packages
task_14.description: Poetry 1.7.0 now preserves package descriptions when it extracts dependency metadata from setup-based projects. This prevents setup.py or setup.cfg packages, especially local path dependencies, from losing their description during dependency resolution or lock file refreshes.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that packages whose metadata is read from setup.py or setup.cfg keep their declared description, so setup-based dependencies do not end up with blank or missing descriptions during dependency resolution and lock updates.

expectation.grounded: Metadata extraction for setup-based packages should return a `description` field alongside `name`, `version`, `install_requires`, `extras_require`, and `python_requires`. When `setup.py` declares a readable string `description` or `setup.cfg` provides `metadata.description`, that value should be surfaced in the extracted metadata; when no description is declared, `description` should remain `None`.
expectation.conceptual: When the library reads dependency metadata from setup-based packages, it should preserve the package description if one is declared and expose it consistently to downstream consumers such as lock generation.

constraints.grounded: This change is additive only: extraction of `name`, `version`, `install_requires`, `extras_require`, and `python_requires` must behave as before, packages without a description must still be readable without error, and absence of a description must not be represented as a fabricated value.
constraints.conceptual: Projects that do not declare a description must continue to work normally, and existing dependency and version parsing behavior must not change as a side effect of adding description support.

behavior: Setup-based metadata extraction now includes `description` in its returned metadata shape.
A declared description in `setup.py` is propagated into extracted package metadata instead of being omitted.
A declared `metadata.description` value in `setup.cfg` is propagated into extracted package metadata instead of being omitted.
If a setup-based package does not declare a description, extracted metadata reports no description while leaving other metadata fields unchanged.
Downstream consumers of extracted metadata, including lockfile generation for local path dependencies, can retain the package description consistently once it is declared in setup-based metadata.
acceptance_criteria: Given a package whose `setup.py` declares a description, when the library extracts that package's metadata, it should return the declared description in the package metadata instead of leaving it blank or missing.
Given a package whose `setup.cfg` declares `metadata.description`, when the library extracts that package's metadata, it should return that description in the package metadata.

Given a setup-based package with no description, when the library extracts metadata, it should still succeed and report no description without altering the parsed name, version, dependency requirements, extras, or Python requirement.

When dependency metadata from a local path package is refreshed for lockfile generation, a declared description from setup-based metadata should remain stable instead of disappearing during extraction.

task_15.title: Ignore inactive extras during dependency resolution
task_15.description: The 1.7.0 update fixes dependency solving for extras so that dependencies reachable only through unselected extras no longer influence version resolution, get locked, or get installed. Only dependencies for the extras that were actually requested should participate in transitive resolution.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that dependency resolution, locking, and installation ignore dependencies that are only activated by extras that were not requested, so inactive extras do not constrain chosen versions or cause additional packages to be installed.

expectation.grounded: For dependencies requested with extras, extra-marked dependency branches must be evaluated against the extras actually selected on that dependency. Branches whose markers are relevant only to inactive extras must be excluded when resolving overlapping dependency markers, while branches still allowed by the current Python constraint and installation environment remain eligible. Dependencies of non-root packages must not be treated as active solely because another extra exists on the package.
expectation.conceptual: Selecting a package without an optional extra should behave as if that extra's dependencies do not exist. Selecting a package with one or more extras should activate only the dependencies for those extras, and unrelated extras must not affect which versions are chosen or which packages are installed.

constraints.grounded: Keep existing marker filtering semantics for Python-version and environment markers. Dependency branches that match an active extra must still participate in resolution, including cases where the same extra has multiple platform- or marker-specific branches. Root-project behavior outside this extra-specific transitive filtering must remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be limited to removing the effect of inactive extras. It must preserve normal resolution for active extras and continue honoring Python and environment conditions for dependencies that are actually in scope.

behavior: Dependencies guarded by an `extra` marker are considered relevant only if that extra was requested on the parent dependency being resolved.
When duplicate dependency declarations are merged across markers, marker combinations that are reachable only through inactive extras are ignored instead of contributing constraints.
Inactive extra branches no longer narrow the solver's version choice for shared transitive dependencies.
Packages required only through inactive extras no longer appear in the locked or installed dependency set.
Dependencies that match an active extra and also satisfy the current Python constraint or environment markers remain part of the resolved dependency graph.
acceptance_criteria: When a dependency is declared without requesting an optional extra, dependencies gated only by that extra should not affect the resolved versions of transitive packages and should not be installed.
When a dependency is declared with a specific extra, only dependencies for the selected extra should participate in resolution; dependencies for other extras should be ignored.
When the same transitive package is required both generally and through an optional extra, resolving without that extra should allow version selection to be driven only by the general requirement.

When an active extra includes multiple marker-restricted branches for the same transitive dependency, the resolver should keep the branches that match the active extra and applicable marker conditions.
When a dependency branch is excluded by the current Python constraint or installation environment, it should continue to be ignored.

task_16.title: Prevent artifact cache races during package downloads
task_16.description: Poetry 1.7.0 fixes a race in artifact caching so concurrent installs and direct URL package handling reliably share a single cached archive. This prevents partial cache files and avoids cases where build requirements fail to install because multiple workers race on the same artifact.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that concurrent installs and source builds do not miss build requirements or consume corrupted cache entries when multiple operations request the same artifact at the same time.

expectation.grounded: When `Executor` or direct-origin URL handling requests an uncached artifact, `ArtifactCache.get_cached_archive_for_link` should support a cache-managed download path for `strict=True` callers by accepting a `download_func`. Concurrent requests for the same link should serialize on a per-archive basis, reuse the same cached file once it exists, and continue to expose the resolved archive path to downstream preparation and installation steps. If the cache-managed download fails, the failure should propagate and any incomplete cached archive should be removed so later operations do not reuse a broken file.
expectation.conceptual: Artifact downloads should behave as one coordinated cache operation. If several install or package-origin flows need the same archive at once, Poetry should end up with one complete cached artifact that all callers can use, and failed downloads should not leave corrupt cache state that can break later installs.

constraints.grounded: Existing cache hits should remain reusable without redownloading. Non-strict archive lookup behavior should remain unchanged. Archive preparation should still use the original cached artifact as the source of hashes and may still select a higher-priority cached archive when available. Download and network failures must still surface to the caller rather than being hidden.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should remove the race without changing normal cache reuse, dependency selection, or error reporting. Successful cached artifacts should keep working as before, and unsuccessful downloads should fail cleanly instead of poisoning the cache.

behavior: `ArtifactCache.get_cached_archive_for_link` can now populate the cache for strict lookups when given a download callback, instead of requiring callers to download the archive outside the cache first.
Concurrent requests for the same artifact are synchronized per cached archive so duplicate downloads do not race to create or overwrite the same file.
If a synchronized download fails, the partially written cached artifact is deleted before the exception is re-raised.
`Executor` now routes original artifact downloads through the artifact cache, so build preparation consumes a cache-managed original archive.
`DirectOrigin.get_package_from_url` now uses the same cache-managed download path for direct URL artifacts instead of performing a separate manual download.
acceptance_criteria: When multiple installation workers request the same uncached artifact concurrently, Poetry should produce one usable cached archive and all requests should resolve against that cached file.

When a source distribution requires build dependencies and the required artifact is fetched concurrently, the build requirements should still be installed instead of being skipped because of cache corruption or a missing archive.
When an artifact download fails while populating the cache, Poetry should raise the download failure and leave no incomplete cached archive for later runs to reuse.
When a requested artifact is already cached, Poetry should reuse the cached archive without forcing another download.
When a direct URL package is resolved, Poetry should use the same coordinated cache behavior as the installer so repeated or concurrent resolutions do not create duplicate or broken downloads.

task_17.title: Respect inherited system site-packages in virtualenv installs
task_17.description: Poetry 1.7.0 fixes dependency detection for virtual environments that include system site-packages. Compatible packages already provided by the underlying Python installation are now recognized as installed so they are not unnecessarily reinstalled into the virtual environment.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when a virtual environment is configured to include system site-packages, compatible dependencies already available from those inherited system packages are treated as installed instead of being installed again into the virtual environment.

expectation.grounded: When `virtualenvs.options.system-site-packages` is enabled for a Poetry-managed virtual environment, installed-package detection must treat distributions located in the virtual environment's library directories and in inherited system site-package directories as installed. If a required dependency is already present there with a compatible version, Poetry should not reinstall it into the virtual environment.
expectation.conceptual: Virtual environments that are allowed to see system packages should reuse compatible inherited dependencies instead of duplicating them. Installation should only add a package when it is missing or the inherited version does not satisfy the requirement.

constraints.grounded: This behavior must remain limited to environments that actually include system site-packages and to distributions found in recognized library directories for the active virtual environment or inherited system site-package locations. Isolated virtual environments must keep existing behavior, and incompatible inherited versions must not prevent installation of an appropriate version.
constraints.conceptual: Do not change how fully isolated virtual environments work, do not treat unrelated filesystem locations as installed packages, and do not skip required installs when the available inherited package version is not acceptable.

behavior: A Poetry virtual environment now distinguishes whether it includes system site-packages and uses that state during installed-package detection.
Installed-package recognition for such a virtual environment now covers both its own library directories and inherited system site-package directories.
System package locations discovered through the active Python installation are considered valid installed-package sources for this check.
As a result, dependency installation no longer reinstalls a package into the virtual environment when a compatible version is already available through inherited system site-packages.
acceptance_criteria: When a Poetry-managed virtual environment is configured with system site-packages enabled and a required dependency already exists in the inherited system packages with a compatible version, running dependency installation should treat that dependency as already installed and should not install a duplicate copy into the virtual environment.
When system site-packages are not enabled for the virtual environment, only packages available from the virtual environment itself should count as installed for dependency installation decisions.

When a dependency is present through inherited system site-packages but its version does not satisfy the declared requirement, installation should still provide a suitable version for the environment.

When an installed distribution is located under a recognized inherited system site-package directory, Poetry should classify it the same way it classifies a distribution installed directly in the virtual environment for purposes of installed-package discovery.

task_18.title: Fix relative git submodule URL resolution
task_18.description: Poetry 1.7.0 fixes installation of git dependencies whose submodules are declared with relative URLs. Relative submodule links are now resolved correctly for SSH and other git URL schemes so recursive dependency cloning targets the intended repositories.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that installing a git dependency correctly resolves and clones submodules declared with relative URLs, including when the parent repository uses SSH or other non-HTTP git URL schemes.

expectation.grounded: When Poetry installs a git dependency and reads submodules from .gitmodules, any submodule URL that is relative and starts with ./ or ../ should be resolved against the dependency's remote URL using URL-path semantics that preserve the original scheme and authority for git transports such as ssh and git+ssh. Absolute submodule URLs should remain unchanged, and resolved submodules should continue to be cloned at the revision recorded in the parent repository index.
expectation.conceptual: Installing a git dependency should recurse into submodules reliably even when those submodules are referenced relative to the parent repository. Users should get the correct submodule repositories and revisions whether the dependency is fetched over HTTPS, SSH, or another supported git transport.

constraints.grounded: Do not change behavior for repositories that do not declare submodules. Do not rewrite absolute submodule URLs. If a configured submodule path is missing from the checked-out repository index, dependency installation should skip that submodule instead of failing unexpectedly.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be limited to incorrect relative submodule resolution and should not regress normal git dependency installs. Existing repositories without affected relative submodule links should continue to behave as before, and missing submodule metadata should not turn into a hard failure.

behavior: Relative submodule URLs are recognized only when the configured submodule URL begins with ./ or ../.

Relative submodule URLs are resolved by joining against the parent repository remote in a way that works for arbitrary git URL schemes, not only schemes treated as relative by the standard library URL join behavior.
Resolving a relative submodule URL preserves the parent remote's non-path URL components while applying relative path traversal to the remote path.
Each discovered submodule is cloned using its resolved URL and the revision stored for that submodule in the parent repository index.
If the repository has no .gitmodules file, no submodules are processed.
If a submodule listed in .gitmodules has no corresponding index entry in the checked-out repository, it is skipped without aborting dependency cloning.
acceptance_criteria: When a git dependency remote uses an SSH-style URL and a submodule URL in .gitmodules is relative, installing the dependency should resolve that submodule to the corresponding SSH-based repository URL and clone it successfully.
When a submodule URL in .gitmodules is already absolute, installing the dependency should use that URL as-is rather than rebasing it onto the parent repository remote.

When a relative submodule URL contains ../ or ./ path traversal, installation should apply that traversal to the parent repository path while preserving the original remote scheme and host information.
When a repository has no submodules, git dependency installation should proceed unchanged.
When .gitmodules references a submodule path that is not present in the repository index, installation should continue without failing because of that missing submodule entry.

task_19.title: Detect failed build dependency installs
task_19.description: Poetry 1.7.0 now detects when installation of a package's build-system dependencies fails in the isolated build environment and reports that failure directly, including diagnostic output, instead of only surfacing a later backend or build failure.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that package installation stops immediately when required build dependencies cannot be installed for an isolated build environment, and report that failure as the direct cause instead of allowing it to appear later as a generic backend or build problem.

expectation.grounded: During installation flows that prepare an isolated build environment, a non-zero result from installing `build-system.requires` must be treated as an immediate failure. The failure should surface as a dedicated `ChefInstallError`, preserve which requirements failed, capture the install step's output and error, and cause `Executor.execute()` to report that the target package's `build-system.requires` could not be installed.
expectation.conceptual: When Poetry cannot install a package's declared build dependencies, it should fail fast and tell the user that the build dependencies could not be installed, along with useful diagnostics from that failed install attempt.

constraints.grounded: Successful installation of `build-system.requires` must continue normally. Dependency resolution problems for `build-system.requires` must remain distinguishable from installation failures, and unrelated package installation errors must continue to be reported as generic package install failures rather than being mislabeled as build dependency install errors.
constraints.conceptual: Do not change successful builds or collapse different failure modes into one. Resolution issues, build-dependency installation issues, and other install failures should remain clearly differentiated.

behavior: Poetry now checks the result of the isolated-environment install step used for `build-system.requires` instead of assuming it succeeded.
If installing `build-system.requires` returns a non-success status, Poetry raises `ChefInstallError` immediately rather than proceeding until a later backend or build failure.
The build-dependency install failure carries the set of requested build requirements and includes captured output and error streams from the failed install attempt.
CLI install reporting now distinguishes build-dependency installation failures from build-dependency resolution failures and from generic package installation failures.
acceptance_criteria: When Poetry installs a package that requires an isolated build environment and the package's build dependencies install successfully, it should continue with normal build preparation.

When installation of a package's `build-system.requires` fails in the isolated environment, the overall package installation should fail immediately and indicate that the package's build-system requirements could not be installed.
When that build-dependency installation failure occurs, the reported diagnostics should identify the failed build requirements and include output captured from the failed install attempt.
When a package's `build-system.requires` cannot be solved, Poetry should report a build-system resolution failure rather than an installation failure.
When installation fails for reasons unrelated to `build-system.requires`, Poetry should continue to report a generic package installation failure.

task_20.title: Fix `poetry shell` behavior in Nushell
task_20.description: Poetry 1.7.0 fixes `poetry shell` integration with Nushell so the virtual environment is activated as soon as the shell opens and interactive commands no longer lose visible keyboard echo.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `poetry shell` works correctly in Nushell by activating the project virtual environment immediately on shell startup and preserving normal interactive terminal input behavior.

expectation.grounded: When `poetry shell` launches a `nu` subshell, it should run the virtual environment activation command as part of the shell invocation so the environment is already active when the prompt appears. For `nu`, `poetry shell` should not disable terminal echo and should not send a second activation command after startup. Existing shell-specific activation behavior for other supported shells should remain unchanged.
expectation.conceptual: Starting `poetry shell` from Nushell should place the user directly into an active project environment, and interactive programs in that shell should behave like a normal terminal with visible typed input.

constraints.grounded: The change is limited to the Nushell path in `poetry shell`. It must eliminate the extra Enter keypress previously needed to finish activation, avoid leaving an activation command waiting at the prompt, and preserve the established activation flow for non-Nushell shells.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should correct Nushell-specific shell startup behavior without altering the expected experience in other shells.

behavior: `poetry shell` now handles Nushell by executing the environment activation during shell startup instead of waiting to inject it after the interactive shell has opened.
In Nushell, the virtual environment is active immediately when the shell prompt appears, without requiring the user to press Enter.
Interactive commands run inside a Nushell session started by `poetry shell` now show typed keyboard input normally because terminal echo remains enabled.
Nushell no longer receives a redundant post-start activation command, so activation text does not remain sitting on the command line.
Behavior for other supported shells remains on their existing shell-specific activation paths.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `poetry shell` from Nushell, the spawned shell should open with the project's virtual environment already active.
When the Nushell prompt appears after `poetry shell`, the user should not need to press Enter to complete activation.
When `poetry shell` opens a Nushell session, it should not leave an activation command visible on the command line waiting to be executed.
When the user runs an interactive program inside a Nushell session started by `poetry shell`, typed input should be echoed normally.
When `poetry shell` is used from other supported shells, their existing activation behavior should continue to work as before.

task_21.title: Clarify missing-value errors for sensitive poetry config settings
task_21.description: Poetry 1.7.0 fixes a confusing CLI failure when `poetry config` is invoked for sensitive settings such as `pypi-token.pypi` without providing a value. The command now reports that the setting requires a value instead of falling through to unrelated no-value handling.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that invoking `poetry config` for sensitive credential-style settings without supplying a value produces a clear missing-value error instead of a confusing or unrelated failure.

expectation.grounded: In `poetry config`, when no `value` argument is provided and `--unset` is not used, keys whose top-level setting belongs to prohibited display/write-only namespaces such as `pypi-token` must raise `ValueError` indicating that the targeted setting requires a value. This validation must apply to nested keys like `pypi-token.pypi` before the command enters its normal no-value display path.
expectation.conceptual: When a user runs `poetry config` for a credential setting like `pypi-token.pypi` without a new value, the CLI should clearly state that the command is incomplete and needs a value, rather than surfacing a misleading error.

constraints.grounded: The missing-value rejection applies only when the command is invoked without a value and without `--unset` for protected setting namespaces. Existing read/show behavior for settings that can be displayed, and explicit unset flows, must remain unaffected by this change.
constraints.conceptual: Normal configuration reads and explicit unsets should continue to work as before. Only incomplete attempts to configure sensitive settings should be rejected with the clearer error behavior.

behavior: Calling `poetry config` with no value for a protected setting namespace such as `pypi-token` now fails immediately with a missing-value `ValueError`.
The missing-value validation applies to nested sensitive keys such as `pypi-token.pypi`, not just the namespace root.
Sensitive no-value invocations no longer fall through to the generic config-display path that previously produced a confusing error.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `poetry config pypi-token.pypi` without a value, the command should fail immediately with a clear indication that the setting requires a value.
When a user runs `poetry config` without a value for a setting that is allowed to be displayed, the command should continue to behave as a read/show operation.
When a user runs `poetry config pypi-token.pypi --unset`, the command should not be blocked by the missing-value validation introduced for no-value invocations.

task_22.title: Handle lockfiles missing metadata gracefully
task_22.description: Poetry 1.7.0 improves lockfile error handling so that a lock file missing its metadata section, including an empty or incomplete lockfile, fails with a clear recovery message instead of a cryptic internal error during lockfile-dependent operations.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that reading a lock file with no metadata section fails with a clear, actionable error instead of a cryptic failure, so users know the lock file must be regenerated.

expectation.grounded: When Poetry reads lock data through `Locker`, any TOML lockfile that lacks the top-level `metadata` entry should raise `RuntimeError` before lock-version parsing. The failure should explicitly indicate that the metadata entry is missing and direct the user to regenerate the lockfile with `poetry lock`.
expectation.conceptual: If a lock file is empty or otherwise missing required metadata, Poetry should stop with a clear error that explains the lock file is incomplete and needs to be rebuilt, rather than surfacing an unhelpful internal failure.

constraints.grounded: This behavior change applies only after the lockfile content has been parsed successfully as TOML. Existing behavior for unreadable or invalid TOML lockfiles must remain intact, and valid lockfiles that include `metadata` must continue through normal version handling without new warnings or altered success behavior.
constraints.conceptual: Do not change how valid lock files behave or how syntax or read errors are reported. Only improve the failure mode for parsed lock files that are structurally missing their metadata section.

behavior: Poetry now detects the absence of the top-level `metadata` section in parsed lock data before accessing lock metadata fields.
When that section is missing, Poetry raises `RuntimeError` with actionable guidance to regenerate the lock file instead of exposing a cryptic missing-key style failure.
Lockfiles that do contain `metadata` continue through the existing lock-version processing path unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: When a `poetry.lock` file parses successfully but has no top-level `metadata` section, any operation that loads the lock data should fail with a clear `RuntimeError` explaining that the metadata is missing and that the lock file should be regenerated.
When the lock file is empty or otherwise incomplete in a way that results in parsed data without `metadata`, Poetry should report the same actionable failure rather than a cryptic internal error.
When the lock file cannot be parsed as valid TOML, Poetry should continue to report the existing read or parse failure behavior.
When the lock file includes a valid `metadata` section, Poetry should continue normal processing with no behavior change introduced by this fix.

task_23.title: Support special-character virtualenv paths
task_23.description: Poetry 1.7.0 fixes encoding-related failures when internal Python helper scripts run inside virtual environments whose paths contain special characters. Environment inspection and PEP 517 metadata generation should keep working under those paths, and command failures should still surface through the existing environment command error flow without exposing the submitted script body.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Poetry can execute its internal Python helper scripts when a virtualenv path contains special or non-ASCII characters, so environment inspection and package metadata extraction do not fail because of script encoding or delivery issues.

expectation.grounded: Poetry should execute inline helper code through `Env.run_python_script()` in a way that remains valid for virtualenv paths containing special characters. Workflows that depend on this helper execution, including `get_pep517_metadata()`, should succeed without relying on stdin-fed `python -` script execution. If one of these subprocesses fails, Poetry should continue to raise `EnvCommandError` with the subprocess output and stderr details, without including the submitted script body in the formatted error.
expectation.conceptual: Operations that depend on running small Python helpers inside a virtual environment should work regardless of special characters in the environment path. Metadata discovery should remain functional, and failures should still be reported as environment command errors with actionable subprocess output.

constraints.grounded: Successful helper-script execution should still return the subprocess stdout expected by Poetry’s environment and metadata routines. Existing command execution semantics should remain intact for normal environment commands, and the fix should remove encoding fragility without requiring users to avoid special-character virtualenv locations.
constraints.conceptual: The update should eliminate path-related encoding failures without changing the normal success and failure contract of environment command execution. Standard workflows should behave the same aside from no longer breaking on special-character virtualenv paths and no longer echoing the helper script text in command errors.

behavior: `get_pep517_metadata()` executes its helper build script through `Env.run_python_script()`, preventing failures caused by feeding the script through standard input in virtual environments whose paths contain special characters.
`Env.run_python_script()` runs inline Python helper code as a command argument rather than stdin input, removing the encoding-sensitive script-delivery path.

`Env.run()` no longer uses a separate stdin-input execution branch for helper scripts; non-call command execution continues to capture subprocess output and converts subprocess failures into `EnvCommandError`.
`EnvCommandError` continues to report subprocess failure details from stdout and stderr, but no longer includes the original helper-script input text.
acceptance_criteria: When a virtual environment path contains special or non-ASCII characters, Poetry operations that execute internal Python helper scripts should complete without encoding-related command failures.
When Poetry performs PEP 517 metadata extraction inside such an environment, it should still obtain package metadata rather than fail because the helper script was passed through stdin.
When an inline helper subprocess fails, Poetry should raise `EnvCommandError` and include any available subprocess stdout and stderr in the reported failure details.
When these helper-script failures are reported, the error details should not include the full submitted script body.

task_25.title: Clarify root project Python range in incompatibility errors
