task_24.title: Align repository connection pools with installer worker limits
task_24.description: Version 1.7.0 fixes a runtime mismatch where HTTP connection pools used for package source access could remain at a separate default size instead of tracking the effective installer worker limit. The upgrade makes installer and repository network clients honor the same capped worker configuration so parallel dependency operations use a matching number of connections.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that configuring installer worker concurrency also adjusts the HTTP connection pool used for package source and repository requests, so parallel dependency operations do not run with a smaller or mismatched pool than their effective worker count.

expectation.grounded: Poetry 1.7.0 should derive one effective worker limit from `Config.installer_max_workers`, using the configured `installer.max-workers` value when present and otherwise Poetry's default worker calculation, then apply that same effective size to the `Executor` and to repository-backed `Authenticator` instances created through `PyPiRepository`, `HTTPRepository`, `LegacyRepository`, `Factory.create_package_source`, and the default repository pool used by `init`.
expectation.conceptual: The configured installer worker limit should consistently govern both parallel work scheduling and the number of HTTP connections available to package sources, including default PyPI access and configured repositories.

constraints.grounded: The effective size must remain capped by Poetry's default maximum worker calculation even when `installer.max-workers` is set higher, and the fallback behavior for platforms where CPU count cannot be determined must remain intact. Disabling installer parallelism must still reduce executor concurrency to a single worker.
constraints.conceptual: This change should only synchronize concurrency-related limits. It must not remove existing worker caps, change fallback behavior on unusual platforms, or alter the single-worker behavior of non-parallel installs.

behavior: When `installer.max-workers` is configured, the effective worker count and repository HTTP connection pool size are derived from the same capped value instead of separate defaults.

When `installer.max-workers` is not configured, Poetry computes the effective size from its platform-based default worker calculation and uses that same value for installer and repository network clients.

Repository clients created for PyPI and other HTTP-based sources now receive the installer-derived pool size, so source access is no longer left at an unrelated default connection-pool size during parallel operations.
If the platform cannot report CPU count, Poetry falls back to its existing default worker calculation and uses that result consistently for the installer-derived pool size.
If installer parallelism is disabled, the executor still operates with one worker.
acceptance_criteria: When a user sets `installer.max-workers` below Poetry's default worker limit and runs dependency operations against PyPI or another HTTP source, the available HTTP connection pool should be reduced to that same effective worker limit instead of remaining at a separate default size.
When a user sets `installer.max-workers` above Poetry's default worker limit, Poetry should cap both the worker count and the associated HTTP connection pool to the same effective maximum.
When `installer.max-workers` is unset, Poetry should use its default worker calculation for both parallel worker scheduling and repository connection pool sizing.
When the platform cannot determine CPU count, Poetry should fall back to its existing default worker calculation and still keep connection pool sizing aligned with that result.
When installer parallelism is disabled, installation execution should continue to run with a single worker.

task_26.title: Prefer pipx in installation guidance
task_26.description: The 1.7.0 update changes installation guidance to present pipx as the preferred installation method, while making isolated-environment usage and CI version pinning more prominent. This is a documentation-only change and does not alter runtime behavior.

behavior: Installation guidance presents `pipx` as the first and preferred method for installing Poetry.

task_28.title: Correct `poetry add` Git dependency example

task_29.title: Clarify auto-included files in build artifacts

task_30.title: Correct repository environment variable documentation

task_31.title: Add standard project citation metadata

task_32.title: Support dynamically generated packages during root install
task_32.description: Poetry should remain compatible with poetry-core 1.7.0 by allowing projects whose package is created by a custom build script to be installed as the current project, while turning missing root-package cases into explicit non-fatal warnings with guidance to skip root installation.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `poetry install` can install projects whose package is created dynamically by a custom build script, and that projects with no installable root package are skipped with a clear warning instead of failing or being silently ignored.

expectation.grounded: During `poetry install`, root project installation should allow the editable build phase to run before package existence is treated as an error, so packages created by a build script are installable. If the root editable install still raises `ModuleOrPackageNotFound` or `FileNotFoundError`, the command should complete successfully, avoid installing the current project, and emit a warning that points users to `--no-root`.
expectation.conceptual: Installing a project that generates its package at build time should work the same as installing a normal packaged project. If the current project is not installable as a package, the install should remain non-fatal and clearly tell the user how to skip root installation.

constraints.grounded: Preserve existing `--no-root` semantics, do not convert missing root-package conditions into hard failures for application-style projects, and do not skip successful editable installs merely because the package is absent until the build script runs.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the opt-out behavior unchanged, avoid breaking projects that are not meant to be installed as packages, and do not regress normal root-package installation flows.

behavior: The root project install flow now handles package discovery after the editable build step, enabling custom build scripts to create the package before installation is validated.
If the editable root install succeeds after the build script runs, the current project is installed instead of being skipped early.
If root installation raises a missing-package or missing-file condition during editable build, the install command exits successfully, skips installing the current project, and surfaces a warning.
Missing root-package cases are no longer silently ignored; users receive guidance to use `--no-root` when they do not want the current project installed.
acceptance_criteria: When a project's package is produced by its custom build script, running `poetry install` without `--no-root` should install the current project successfully.

task_33.title: Correct multi-extra marker handling
task_33.description: The upgrade fixes how dependency markers using `extra` are interpreted. `extra` is now treated as a multi-valued marker during validation, extra names are normalized before comparison, and marker-combination logic no longer collapses different extra clauses as if they were mutually exclusive. This preserves optional dependency conditions when one or more extras are active.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that dependency markers using `extra` are evaluated correctly when multiple extras can be active at the same time, so optional dependency conditions are not incorrectly simplified, rejected, or mismatched because of extra-name normalization.

expectation.grounded: Marker handling should treat `extra` as a special multi-valued marker. Validation of `extra` conditions should accept the environment's `extra` value as either a single extra name or a collection of active extras, canonicalize both the active extras and the marker's extra value, and evaluate `==` and `!=` as membership checks against that normalized set. Marker combination behavior for `extra`, including intersection and union of parsed markers, should only simplify when the compared extra value is the same; combinations involving different extra values must remain explicit combined marker expressions instead of being collapsed as impossible or redundant.
expectation.conceptual: Extra-based dependency conditions should behave like checks against the full set of active extras, not like checks against a single scalar field. If several extras are enabled, conditions that refer to multiple extras should remain satisfiable when appropriate, and equivalent spellings of an extra should match each other.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the existing single-valued semantics for non-`extra` markers. For `extra`, contradictory checks on the same normalized extra should still remain unsatisfiable, duplicate same-value checks may still collapse, and different extra values must not be treated as mutually exclusive during marker simplification. Explicitly provided active extras must drive the result of `extra` validation.
constraints.conceptual: Keep ordinary platform, Python, and other marker behavior unchanged. Only extras should be treated as multi-select values, and only truly conflicting conditions on the same extra should be considered impossible.

behavior: Validation of `extra` markers supports either a single active extra or multiple active extras.
`extra == name` succeeds when the normalized extra name is present in the active extra set, and `extra != name` succeeds when it is absent.
Equivalent extra names match after normalization, even if their original spelling differs by case or punctuation normalization.
Combining markers with different `extra` values via intersection preserves a conjunctive marker instead of simplifying it to an impossible result.
Combining markers with different `extra` values via union preserves a disjunctive marker instead of collapsing it away.
An explicitly empty active-extra collection behaves as no extras selected for `extra` membership checks.
acceptance_criteria: When marker validation receives active extras such as `a` and `b`, a condition that requires both `extra == a` and `extra == b` should evaluate as satisfied.
When marker validation receives active extras that do not include `a`, `extra == a` should evaluate as unsatisfied and `extra != a` should evaluate as satisfied.
When a marker refers to an extra whose spelling differs only by normalization from an active extra, the comparison should still match.
When intersecting markers that refer to different extras, the result should continue to represent both extra requirements rather than being treated as impossible.
When unioning markers that refer to different extras, the result should continue to represent either extra as acceptable rather than being reduced to a single value or unconditional truth.
When the active extra collection is explicitly empty, equality checks against extras should be unsatisfied and inequality checks against extras should be satisfied.

task_35.title: Restore editable installs for projects with extension modules
task_35.description: Editable installs for projects that ship extension modules should work correctly. constraints.grounded: Limit the changed behavior to editable wheel builds. Standard non-editable wheel builds must continue packaging extension outputs normally. Editable wheels must preserve existing `.pth`-based editable semantics rather than relying on bundling built package files into the wheel.
constraints.conceptual: Do not regress normal wheel builds or change editable installs into full packaged installs. Keep the fix scoped to making editable installs of extension-based projects behave correctly.

behavior: Editable wheel creation for projects with extension modules now builds the extension artifact in place so it is available from the source checkout.
Editable wheels for such projects continue to include the source-linking `.pth` metadata used for editable installs.
During editable builds, poetry-core no longer depends on copying the built package directory from the temporary build output into the wheel.
The resulting editable wheel omits the packaged project tree, avoiding a duplicate non-editable copy inside the editable artifact.

task_34.title: Refresh supported SPDX license resolution
task_34.description: The library refreshes its bundled SPDX license catalog so additional upstream license and exception identifiers are recognized as known licenses during project parsing and metadata generation, improving canonical license normalization for users who declare those newly added SPDX entries.

task_36.title: Fix wheel build lib directory selection
task_36.description: The 1.7.0 update fixes wheel packaging so generated build artifacts are taken from explicit purelib or platform-specific build output directories instead of guessing from lib folder name patterns. synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that wheel builds include files from the correct build output directory so packages do not ship the wrong files, or miss generated files entirely, when the build process produces either pure-Python or platform-specific library output.

If neither directory exists because no build artifacts were produced, wheel creation should continue without treating that as an error.
expectation.conceptual: Wheel packaging should deterministically collect generated build artifacts from the correct build output location, regardless of platform-specific naming differences, and should avoid failing when no generated build output is present.

constraints.grounded: Preserve successful wheel builds for both pure-Python and platform-specific distributions, avoid selecting an arbitrary build lib directory based on glob matching, and keep the no-artifacts case non-fatal when a conditional build step produces nothing to copy.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should improve reliability of packaged wheel contents without changing expected behavior for builds that already produce correct outputs, and it should not turn optional build outputs into hard failures.

behavior: Wheel builds use explicit purelib and platform-specific build output directories instead of relying on implicit build lib naming.
If a platform-specific build output directory is present, wheel packaging copies artifacts from that directory.
If no platform-specific build output exists but a purelib build output directory exists, wheel packaging copies artifacts from the purelib directory.

acceptance_criteria: When a wheel build produces generated files only in the pure-Python build output directory, the resulting wheel should include those generated files.
When a wheel build produces platform-specific outputs in the platform-specific build output directory, the resulting wheel should include those outputs.

When a build step produces no build output directory, the wheel build should still succeed without attempting to package nonexistent artifacts.

task_37.title: Support exporting all Poetry extras with a single flag
task_37.description: The export command now supports including every declared extra dependency set through a single option, so users no longer need to keep an explicit extra list in sync as projects evolve. synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `poetry export` can include dependencies from every declared extra without requiring users to enumerate each extra manually, and reject conflicting requests that try to combine automatic all-extra export with explicit extra selection.

expectation.grounded: The `poetry export` command should expose a `--all-extras` option that includes all extras declared by the package in the exported output. When `--all-extras` is provided together with `--extras` or `-E`, the command should report the conflict and exit with a non-zero status instead of exporting. Existing validation for explicitly named extras should remain in place, so unknown extras passed through `--extras` continue to be rejected.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to export a lockfile with all optional dependency extras in one command, so new extras are picked up automatically without changing automation or deployment commands. The export command should treat automatic inclusion of all extras and manual extra selection as mutually exclusive modes.

constraints.grounded: The new behavior must not change how exports work when no extras are requested. Explicit `--extras` handling should keep its current validation semantics, except that it cannot be combined with `--all-extras`. Other export settings, such as format and dependency-group selection, should continue to behave as before when `--all-extras` is used.
constraints.conceptual: The added flag should extend extra-selection behavior without altering unrelated export workflows. Invalid or ambiguous user input should be rejected clearly rather than silently reinterpreted.

behavior: `poetry export` provides a new `--all-extras` option for including every declared extra dependency set in the export.
Using `--all-extras` causes the export to include dependencies contributed by all extras defined by the project, including extras added after existing export commands were written.
Using `--all-extras` together with `--extras` or `-E` is treated as an invalid combination and the command exits with status code 1.
Explicit extra selection through `--extras` keeps its existing behavior, including rejection of unknown extra names.
acceptance_criteria: When a project defines multiple extras and the user runs `poetry export --all-extras`, the exported output should include dependencies from all declared extras.
When a project later adds another extra, rerunning `poetry export --all-extras` should include that extra without requiring the command invocation to change.
When the user runs `poetry export --all-extras` together with `--extras` or `-E`, the command should fail instead of producing an export.
When the user explicitly requests an unknown extra through `--extras`, the command should continue to reject the request.

task_38.title: Export Git dependencies with resolved commit hashes
task_38.description: The export flow now pins Git-based dependencies to the exact resolved commit recorded in the lock data instead of emitting a branch name or other symbolic reference. This makes exported requirements and constraints files reflect the concrete locked revision and improves reproducibility for downstream installs.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that exporting dependencies produces Git-based requirements pinned to the exact resolved commit recorded in the lock data, rather than a branch name or other unresolved reference.

expectation.grounded: When `poetry export` generates `requirements.txt` or `constraints.txt`, Git/VCS dependencies should be serialized from their resolved locked reference so the exported requirement points to the concrete commit hash instead of the original branch or alias. Any existing environment markers on that dependency should still be present in the exported line.
expectation.conceptual: Exported dependency files should describe the exact Git revision that was locked, not a moving branch label, so installs based on the export remain reproducible and consistent with the lock state.

constraints.grounded: Only the rendering of remote Git/VCS dependency references should change. Export behavior for version-pinned packages, local file or directory dependencies, editable compatibility rules, hash emission, and index URL handling should remain unchanged apart from using the resolved VCS reference where applicable.
constraints.conceptual: This update should only correct how Git dependencies are pinned in exported files. Other dependency formatting and export behavior should stay consistent with prior releases.

behavior: `poetry export` now emits Git/VCS dependency entries using the resolved commit hash stored in the lock information instead of a branch name or other symbolic reference.
The resolved-reference behavior applies to both supported text export formats, `requirements.txt` and `constraints.txt`.
If an exported Git dependency also carries environment markers, the markers remain attached while the dependency target is pinned to the resolved commit.
acceptance_criteria: When a project contains a Git dependency locked from a branch or symbolic revision, exporting `requirements.txt` should produce a Git requirement pinned to the resolved commit hash rather than the branch or symbolic revision name.
When the same locked Git dependency is exported to `constraints.txt`, the exported entry should also point to the resolved commit hash.
When an exported Git dependency has environment markers, the exported line should preserve those markers while using the resolved commit hash.
When exporting dependencies that are not Git/VCS-based, their export format should remain unchanged by this fix.
